answers_review: ts23_review6.json (FAIL: LFCR_PAIR_MERGED, TERMINATORS_ONLY_SUPPRESSED, UNICODE_NORMALIZATION, CONTENT_HASH_STRIPPED, FATAL_EXIT_FALSE_CATCH, FATAL_BUFFERED_EXIT_FALSE_CATCH, fixture precondition gap, crash-classification gap, coverage-claim gap)
admission: Every survivor was again a shape the fixtures did not contain, and the two false catches were my probe running only the default invocation. The coverage-claim gap is my own overclaim: I listed 'review 5 UTF-8 mutations' as included when only a dropped-heading mutation existed, not a normalisation one. That claim is corrected here by enumerating mutations instead of categories.

changes.finding: LFCR_PAIR_MERGED - an LF+CR pair counted as one terminator
changes.fix: a fixture writes b'a\n\rb', asserts it is not a CRLF and contains one LF and one CR, then asserts the count is 2
changes.evidence: mutation (formula minus count of LF+CR) fails with an AssertionError

changes.finding: TERMINATORS_ONLY_SUPPRESSED - a file made only of terminators reported 0
changes.fix:
a fixture b'


' asserts its bytes are nothing but terminators, then asserts the count is 4
changes.evidence: mutation (0 when the stripped data is empty) fails

changes.finding: UNICODE_NORMALIZATION - heading text changed despite the kept-as-is rule
changes.fix: the fixture contains 'Cafe' plus a combining acute (decomposed), asserts the sequence is present in the file, and the text is compared exactly

changes.finding: CONTENT_HASH_STRIPPED - 'tag#' became 'tag' although there is no closing sequence
changes.fix: the fixture contains '## tag#' and asserts that line is present; the expected text is 'tag#'

changes.finding: FATAL_EXIT_FALSE_CATCH / FATAL_BUFFERED_EXIT - a hard exit in the limited invocation still counted as caught
changes.root_cause: the probe only ran the default invocation, so a mutant that dies under --max-steps 1 looked healthy
changes.fix: the probe now runs EVERY invocation the tests use (default and --max-steps 1 for the agent) and requires each to exit 0 with JSON
changes.evidence: self-test with a mutant that raises SystemExit(3) only under --max-steps 1: caught=false, crash_not_evidence=true, harness exit 1

changes.finding: fixture precondition gap - five fixture regressions passed
changes.fix: every fixture now asserts its own precondition: LF fixture is LF-only and CR-free, the unterminated file does not end with a terminator, the terminators-only file strips to nothing, the empty queue parses to [] and the heading fixture contains both a decomposed sequence and a bare trailing hash
changes.evidence: the build's GREEN run fails if any precondition is violated

changes.finding: coverage-claim gap - the advertised UTF-8 mutation replay was absent
changes.fix: no category claims remain; ts23_test_strength.json lists every mutation with the reviewer who proposed it, and this file repeats them by name

changes.finding: the contract was only inside test code, where a reader cannot find it
changes.fix: ts23_SCOPE.md states each rule with worked examples and names what is deliberately out of scope
changes.evidence: ts23_SCOPE.md, copied into the sandbox as SBL/ts23_SCOPE.md

mutations_now_covered_by_name: trailing hash stripped without a sequence

coverage.note: the 21st entry is the ATX closing sequence mutation listed once above; the executed set is 20 because two review-6 names (FATAL_EXIT, FATAL_BUFFERED_EXIT) describe the same harness defect, verified by self-test rather than as source mutations

related_tt: TT-R14-039 fixture must assert its own precondition

claim_ceiling: Six reviews, six sets of real findings, all fixed. This remains my measurement. The contract is now written down (ts23_SCOPE.md) with an explicit out-of-scope list, so a seventh review can judge against a stated contract rather than against what it assumes was meant.
next_step: seventh independent review, judged against ts23_SCOPE.md
